//Jwt: Jwt:Key is empty on purpose: a token signing key must never be committed. Supply the real key through the host's secret store, i.e. the Jwt__Key environment variable. Generate it with: dotnet user-secrets set "Jwt:Key" "$(openssl rand -base64 48)" locally, or a fresh 64-char random string in production. The API refuses to start without it.
//ConnectionStrings: The SQL credential is NOT stored in this file or anywhere in git. Provide it out-of-band as ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection. It must be the credential rotated after the previous one was exposed, and it must encrypt the transport: 'Server=<sql-host>; Database=<db>; User Id=<login>; Password=<rotated-password>; Encrypt=True; TrustServerCertificate=True; MultipleActiveResultSets=True;'. Drop TrustServerCertificate once the host presents a certificate issued by a CA the web server machine trusts. The API refuses to start when this is missing, and refuses to start in a non-Development environment if the string asks for Encrypt=False. See DEPLOYMENT.md.
//Cors: Origins allowed to call this API from a browser with credentials. The staff web app is deployed to a different runasp.net site, so its origin must be listed here or the SignalR hub and every fetch() from notifications.js fails. Deployed origins are not secret, so they live in this file; extra environments go in the Cors__AllowedOrigins__2 environment variable.
//Bootstrap: The application creates NO demo data. The first System Administrator is created once, only when the user table is completely empty, from these values. Leave them blank here and supply real values as environment variables (Bootstrap__AdminEmail / Bootstrap__AdminPassword / Bootstrap__AdminName) so no credential is committed to source control. Change the password and delete the variables after first sign-in.
//Email: SMTP for the three notices this system sends by itself: an account decision, an email-confirmation link and a password-reset link. Every value is blank here and comes from the host's secret store (Email__Host / Email__Port / Email__UseSsl / Email__Username / Email__Password / Email__FromAddress / Email__FromName) so no mail credential is committed. While Email__Host is empty each message is logged instead of sent - the development case, and also the fail-safe: an approval or a new password is recorded whether or not the mail server answers.
//Sites: The origin the emailed links are built against. Reset and confirmation pages belong to the web app rather than to this API - a form served from the API would have nowhere to post back to - so the link uses the web site's origin. Deployed origins are not secret and are already listed in Cors. Run the web app somewhere else and override it with Sites__WebBaseUrl, e.g. http://localhost:5253.
